To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the run-up of the major δ13C excursions of the Phanerozic is often accompanied by high abundance of acritarchs with abnormal forms.

(1) abnormal forms of marine protists are often associated with the onset of global carbon cycle perturbutions, (2) this implies that the perturbations were somehow related to a change of environmental conditions, and (3) the change of the environmental conditions was probably caused by a change of the ambient sea-water composition.

(1) the run-up of major δ 13C excursions is characterized by high abundances of malformed acritarchs; (2) the cause of this is still unknown; (3) the cause is possibly related to environmental stress, and (4) the cause is not related to the carbon cycle itself, but to the carbon cycle as a proxy for environmental stress
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether or not the high abundances of abnormal forms of acritarch species are a response to a global environmental stress.
the search for a common cause of the global carbon isotope excursions and of the contemporaneous extinction/turnover events of several marine invertebrate groups.
the search for the causal mechanisms of the perturbations of carbon isotope composition of sea water, and with their impact on marine ecosystems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

high abundances and/or occurrences of abnormal forms of acritarch taxa are coeval to the onset and run-up of major positive carbon isotope excursions, and that they may therefore be used to define the base of such events in stratigraphic sections.

the onset of major carbon cycle perturbances in the Early Palaeozoics is characterised by the occurrence of high abundances of abnormal acritarch forms, which may be related to the carbon isotopic composition and the ambient sea water.
high abundances (and possibly the occurrence) of teratological acritarchs is a reliable proxy for the onset of a δ 13 C carbon excursion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the run-up of the δ 13 C isotope excursions is accompanied by a strong environmental stress that is reflected by high abundances of abnormal forms in several groups of marine protists.
the onset of global δ 13 C perturbations is accompanied by a high degree of stress in the environment, which is expressed by the occurrence of abnormal forms of marine microplankton.
the occurrence of teratological acritarchs may be an important indicator for environmental stress, and thus for environmental changes, which may be linked to global carbon cycle perturbances.
